arabic text: Arman tha ye maa kaa, me sehra sajawungi
english translation text: O my young Akbar—your mother longed to adorn your wedding crown.

arabic text: Shaadi ko teri mujhko mehndi bhi lagani thi Zalim ne magar\nhaaye hathon me rasan bandhi Maine to yeh socha tha Me kangna\nbandhaungi
english translation text: For your wedding I wished to apply henna,\nbut the tyrant bound my hands in rope.\nI had imagined I would tie bracelets upon your wrists.

arabic text: Jab ghar se chale the tum, sughra se kiya waada Beemar meri\nbehna, mein lot ke aawunga Kis tarha khabar jaakar, sughra ko\nsunawungi
english translation text: When we left home, you promised Sughra:\nmy ailing sister, I will return.\nHow will I go and tell Sughra the news?

arabic text: Bete ke janaze ko kab baap uthata hai\nKitna hi bahadur ho woh jee nahi sakta hai Lekin tere baba ki,\nhimmat me barhaungi
english translation text: When does a father ever lift his son's funeral bier?\nHowever brave he may be, he cannot survive such grief.\nYet I will strengthen your father's courage.

arabic text: Jaate ho chale jawo, mei rok nahi sakti\nIk waada karo lekin aur khawo qasam meri Tum lot ke aawoge jis\nwaqt bulawungi
english translation text: Go if you must; I cannot stop you.\nBut make me one promise and swear by me:\nwhen I call you, you will return.

arabic text: Jab dulha banoge tum me dungi tera sadqa Mujhko teri dulhan ko\nseene se lagana tha Ab tere janaze ko seene se lagaungi
english translation text: When you became a bridegroom, I would have offered charity for you.\nI wished to embrace your bride. Now I will embrace your funeral bier.

arabic text: Laaye hai tera laasha khaime me tere baba Armaan hazaron the\nsab khaak huwe beta Me apni tamana ki khud qabr banawungi
english translation text: Your father has brought your body into the tents. Thousands of hopes have turned\nto dust, my son. I will make a grave for my own longings.

arabic text: Dekho to karim aakar tum karbobala manzar Ik laashe jawaan hai\naur deti hai sada madar Mein phool ko sehre ke turbat pe\nbichawungi
english translation text: O Karim, come and behold the scene of Karbala:\na young man's body lies there, while his mother cries:\nI will scatter the wedding flowers over your grave.
